rationale:
Evidence from the iteration-4 race (base_speed 1.1, wide span x = ±0.07 m): line_loss_events fell to 0 on oval and s-bend and stayed at 1 only on slalom. Max_error was 0.0611 to 0.0614 on oval and s-bend, still just above the 0.06 m off-track limit, and 0.0694 on slalom. Progress stayed low (oval 0.115, s-bend 0.040, slalom 0.105). Lowering speed from 1.4 to 1.1 barely moved max_error, so speed is not the main cause, as the approved candidate's feedback anticipated. Kp, ki and kd changes have not moved max_error either, and max_error is pinned near 0.061 on every track. Widening the body cannot clear the limit: body_width would need to exceed about 0.19 m, above the 0.18 m maximum.

Decision: keep base_speed 1.1, the wide span, kp 2.0, ki 0.4, kd 0.15 and last_direction, and make one geometry change. Move the sensor row from y = 0.05 m to y = 0.02 m, closer to the axle, following the approved feedback's plan. The hypothesis is that the lateral excursion starts at the drive-wheel and body rotation, so the sensors' reach relative to the axle sets the early error. Moving the array changes that reach.

Expected result: max_error drops below 0.06 on at least s-bend and oval, and progress rises above the iteration-4 values. Risk: the sensors may see the line later, which could increase line-loss events on slalom. Hypotheses to check: H1, max_error is set by the sensor y position relative to the axle, so y = 0.02 changes it; H2, if max_error is still about 0.061 at y = 0.02, the cause is the kd or the start transient, and kd 0.3 is the next single-variable test.

Measurements wanted: max_error and rms_error per track, line_loss_events, progress, completion, steering_oscillation and completion_time.
